answer: In this PoA design, identity verification uses a Wesolowski VDF: every valid response requires a fixed chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result needed for the next. Cloned identities cannot collapse that dependency chain or gain a speedup by spreading one proof across GPUs; parallel machines only repeat the same wall-clock cost per clone. The velvet lure of mass identities therefore meets a basalt-hard bottleneck that forges a time-bound, verifiable identity.
